name: Bloom Energy Corporation
business_summary: Bloom Energy makes solid-oxide fuel cell power systems that generate electricity on site, sold mainly as product, installation and service, and also offers solid-oxide electrolyzers. More and more of its new business comes from AI data centers through large frameworks with Oracle and Brookfield. It reports a single segment.
main_products: Solid-oxide fuel cell power systems (Energy Servers) for on-site/behind-the-meter power
ai_energy_commodity_link: Company-stated: Bloom positions its fuel cells as fast behind-the-meter power for AI data centers. Oracle intends to procure up to 2.8 GW under a master services agreement, with 1.2 GW contracted and being deployed (Apr 13, 2026 release). Brookfield's AI-infrastructure financing framework with Bloom grew from up to $5B (Oct 2025) to $25B (Jun 30, 2026), but no specific new sites or customers were named. Measurable: Q2 2026 revenue was $1,065.4M (+165.5% y/y), of which product revenue was $935.4M. FY2025 10-K: three customers made up ~43%, 13% and 12% of revenue, and the largest is a related party. No data-center share of revenue was seen in any filing. Commodity exposure: the systems typically run on natural gas (background knowledge; not quantified here). Scandium oxide is a key input and is the subject of short-seller allegations.

confirmed_relationships.detail: Master services agreement under which Oracle intends to procure up to 2.8 GW of Bloom fuel cell systems for U.S. projects; initial 1.2 GW contracted with deployment underway and continuing into next year

name: Ero Copper Corp.
country_hq: Canada (Vancouver, British Columbia); operations in Brazil
business_summary: Ero Copper is a copper-focused miner whose operations are all in Brazil: the Caraíba Operations (Bahia), the Tucumã Operation (Pará; commercial production July 2025) and the NX Gold Xavantina gold operations. It is also earning a 60% interest in Vale Base Metals' Furnas copper-gold project. It sells copper concentrate and gold.
main_products: Silver/gold by-products in copper concentrate (by-product detail not verified)
ai_energy_commodity_link: Measurable commodity exposure: copper production was 17,315 t in concentrate in Q2 2026 (C1 $2.42/lb), and FY2026 guidance is 67,500-77,500 t. Gold from Xavantina was 20,553 oz in Q2 2026. Revenue and earnings are driven by copper and gold prices, with Brazil-only operations (BRL cost exposure is background knowledge, not quantified here). No company statement linking revenue to AI data centers was seen. Any AI/electrification link is indirect, through copper demand.

confirmed_relationships.detail: Furnas Copper-Gold Project earn-in: Ero can earn 60% by completing exploration, engineering and development milestones over 5 years. name: Ivanhoe Mines Ltd.
country_hq: Canada (Vancouver, British Columbia); assets in DRC and South Africa
business_summary: Ivanhoe Mines develops and operates mines in Africa. Its main assets are the Kamoa-Kakula copper complex in the DRC (a joint venture with Zijin and the DRC government, with an on-site smelter), the Kipushi zinc mine in the DRC, and the Platreef PGM-nickel-copper-gold mine in South Africa, which began Phase 1 production in Nov 2025. Kamoa-Kakula is equity-accounted, so consolidated revenue mainly reflects Kipushi.
main_products: PGMs (3PE+Au), nickel and copper in concentrate (Platreef)
segments: Kamoa-Kakula (joint venture; share of profit, equity-accounted)
ai_energy_commodity_link: Measurable commodity exposure: Kamoa-Kakula (100% basis) sold 61,249 t of payable copper in Q2 2026 at an average realized $5.99/lb, for revenue of $880M (including $56M of sulphuric acid sales). Kipushi produced a record 70,177 t of zinc in Q2 2026. Ivanhoe's consolidated revenue is only $152.6M because Kamoa-Kakula is a joint venture. The company tightened 2026 Kamoa-Kakula guidance to 290-310 kt copper. Energy: an on-site hybrid solar and battery facility cut diesel-generator use by 40% in Sep 2026 (secondary report). No company statement linking revenue to AI data centers was seen. The AI link is only indirect, through copper demand.

name: Cameco Corporation
business_summary: Cameco is a uranium producer (McArthur River/Key Lake and Cigar Lake in Saskatchewan, plus a share of JV Inkai in Kazakhstan) and a nuclear fuel services provider (conversion, CANDU fuel). It owns 49% of Westinghouse Electric with Brookfield and equity-accounts the stake. It sells mainly to nuclear utilities under long-term contracts.
main_products: Fuel services: UF6 conversion, UO2 and CANDU fuel fabrication
Westinghouse (49%): reactor technology (AP1000), nuclear fuel and plant services
ai_energy_commodity_link: Measurable: revenue depends on uranium volumes and realized prices under long-term utility contracts. ~230 Mlb were committed under long-term contracts at end-2025 (call summary). FY2026 guidance is revenue C$3,320-3,570M and 19.5-21.5 Mlb of production (Cameco share). Energy policy link: Westinghouse is central to the US government framework for at least US$80B of new reactors (Oct 2025 binding term sheet) and a DOE conditional commitment of up to US$17.5B for AP1000 long-lead items (Jun 2026). AI data-center demand appears only in secondary commentary (e.g., Motley Fool). No company-disclosed AI-linked revenue was seen.

confirmed_relationships.detail: Co-owner of Westinghouse (Cameco 49%, Brookfield the remainder) and co-party to the US government reactor-deployment partnership

Binding term sheet: the US government arranges financing and facilitates permitting for new Westinghouse reactors with aggregate value of at least US$80B. Its participation interest (once vested) gives 20% of Westinghouse cash distributions above US$17.5B. It can require an IPO (with a 20% warrant) if valuation is expected to be ≥$30B by Jan 2029. Definitive agreements are still pending
